description: How telecommunication networks carry voice and data at scale: an overview of network structure, switching and signalling, transmission systems, optical-fibre and satellite communication, traffic engineering, and the regulation of telecommunications. Taught with browser-based simulations of links, switches and traffic loads, so students dimension networks, model blocking and trace a call or packet across the network without physical equipment.
modelledOn: Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
ITU-T recommendations and the ITU radio regulations
outcomes: Describe the structure of a telecommunication network from access to core.
Explain circuit and packet switching and the signalling that sets up and controls connections.
Analyse transmission systems in terms of bandwidth, multiplexing, modulation and impairments.
Explain optical-fibre and satellite links and when each is the right choice.
Apply traffic engineering to dimension a network and estimate blocking and quality of service.
Describe how telecommunications are regulated and how spectrum and licensing are managed.

units.title: Telecommunication networks overview
